record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.context_brief: Products of toric diagrams and B-models
record.original_question: Graded quivers can be constructed from the topological B-model, and products of toric diagrams produce higher-dimensional Gorenstein singularities from lower-dimensional ones. Is there a correspondence between the product construction for toric diagrams and B-model approaches to graded quivers?

evidence.quote: Question 21. Graded quivers can be obtained from the topological B-model. Can we find any correspondence between the product of toric diagrams and the B-model approaches?

artifact.category_tag: graded quivers and toric Gorenstein singularities
artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graded quiver with superpotential of order m+1 consists of a finite quiver Q whose arrows carry an integer grading c ∈ {1,2,…,m}, together with a superpotential W that is a formal sum of cycles satisfying a grading condition (degree m+1) and modulo signed cyclic equivalence. Such graded quivers arise as the open-string sector of the topological B-model on local Calabi–Yau (m+2)-fold singularities; in particular, for toric Gorenstein (m+2)-fold singularities X, the associated graded quiver theory can be derived from a B-model construction on X. 

On the other hand, there is a purely combinatorial product operation on toric diagrams: given a Gorenstein toric singularity X of complex dimension d₁ with toric diagram Δ₁ ⊂ ℤ^{d₁-1} and another Gorenstein toric singularity Y of complex dimension d₂ with toric diagram Δ₂ ⊂ ℤ^{d₂-1}, one forms a (d₁+d₂−1)-dimensional toric Gorenstein singularity whose toric diagram Δ₁ × Δ₂ is obtained by an appropriate fibered product of the two diagrams. This product lifts to a construction on the corresponding graded quivers with superpotential, producing a graded quiver associated to Δ₁ × Δ₂ from those associated to Δ₁ and Δ₂.

Problem: Establish a precise correspondence, intrinsic to the topological B-model, between the combinatorial product of toric diagrams and the B-model construction of graded quivers. Concretely, given the B-model graded-quiver data for Gorenstein toric singularities X and Y, identify a B-model operation that produces the graded-quiver data attached to the product toric singularity X × Y (in the sense of the toric-diagram product above), and prove that the resulting graded quiver with superpotential coincides, up to the relevant equivalence, with the one obtained by the combinatorial product of the two graded quivers.
artifact.status_search_result: This is posed as one of several open questions about graded quiver gauge theories associated with Gorenstein singularities; no published resolution establishing a B-model correspondence with the toric-diagram product construction was found, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
status_evidence.snippet: List of open questions concerning graded quivers, toric diagrams, and B-model constructions.
status_evidence.claim: The question is stated as an unresolved open problem.
